problems.form_value: Number of accurate hypotheses (listed teams whose playoff betting odds favored qualification)
problems.source_says: The PDF says accurate hypotheses were identified using contemporaneous playoff betting odds, but does not state the decision rule that converts those odds into an accurate/inaccurate classification. The more specific claim that qualification had to be favored is therefore unverified; SI Table S1 is unavailable. The reported count statistics themselves match the PDF.
problems.quote: We identified accurate hypotheses based on the playoff betting odds of teams at the time of the experiment, publicly available on the Internet (SI Appendix, Table S1).
problems.locator: PDF p. 5, Paradigm, paragraph beginning We also assessed; SI Appendix Table S1 is cited but not included.

problems.source_says: The analyzed outcome is a participant's proportion of accurate hypotheses, derived by dividing two counts. Its formula in measure_detail is correct. However, codebook section 6 defines category_count as counts of ideas, categories, or unique ideas, and does not explicitly include proportions derived from counts. The categorical measure label cannot be confirmed under that definition; a convention allowing normalized counts, or a null pending resolution, is needed. This does not undermine scored_on_output or the participant unit.
problems.quote: percent accuracy (i.e., actual hit rate; number of correct hypotheses divided by number of total hypotheses generated)
problems.locator: PDF p. 8, LLMs do not reduce accuracy but do reduce confidence in hypotheses, first sentence; p. 9, Fig. 4(b); creativity-codebook.md section 6, Measure.

problems.source_says: The ancillary experiment has only a brief task description and a directional result in this PDF. These support the occupation-guessing hypothesis-count outcome and its reported direction, but do not explicitly describe how the count was obtained, whether it was scored from submitted outputs, or whether AI was available during the scored generation rather than at another stage. Immediate timing is also unstated. These method and timing fields remain unverified without SI Section 5; null is preferable to asserting them as confirmed. The existing not_stated unit is appropriately cautious.
problems.quote: participants guessed the (single) occupation of a person after reading a brief profile description. Again, using LLMs increased the number of hypotheses that participants generated.
problems.locator: PDF p. 11, Discussion, paragraph beginning Our paradigm controlled; SI Appendix Section 5 is cited but not included.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1: The investigators counted unique teams in submitted lists, supporting output scoring, fluency, category_count, participant, with_ai and immediate AI availability; all reported means, SDs, t, p, d and total N match.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, Paradigm and Results, Experiment 1; p. 12, Experiment 1 procedure.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2: Accurate hypotheses are computed from submitted teams against betting odds, supporting output scoring, other, category_count and participant with AI available; all reported numerical statistics match.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, accuracy paragraph and Experiment 1 results; p. 12, Experiment 1 procedure.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3: Actual hit rate is an objective participant-level proportion of submitted teams, with AI available during generation; Fig. 4(b) shows the LLM mean slightly lower and overlapping 95% CIs, as recorded.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5 and 8, accuracy definitions; p. 9, Fig. 4(b), Exp1 row.

confirmed.statement: S1-O4: The authors count unique hypotheses across all participants in each crowd, supporting diversity, category_count, set and across_people; the text reports no difference without numerical estimates.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Homogeneity of hypotheses generated with and without LLMs; pp. 4-5 and 12, AI instructions.

confirmed.statement: S2-O1: Unique listed teams are the participant-level fluency outcome produced with Google Bard available; all recorded means, SDs, t, p, d and total N match.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Experiment 2 results; p. 6, Fig. 1; p. 13, Experiment 2 procedure.

confirmed.statement: S2-O2: The accurate-hypothesis count is computed on participants submitted lists with AI available; its participant unit, other construct and category_count measure are supported, and all numerical statistics match.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, accuracy definition and Experiment 2 results; p. 13, Experiment 2 procedure.

confirmed.statement: S2-O3: Actual hit rate is an objective participant-level proportion with AI available; the Exp2 means in Fig. 4(b) nearly coincide, and no per-experiment numerical test is printed.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, accuracy definition; p. 9, Fig. 4(b), Exp2 row; p. 13, procedure.

confirmed.statement: S2-O4: The aggregate unique-team count compares different participants outputs, supporting diversity, category_count, set and across_people; numerical results are referred to SI Table S21.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Homogeneity of hypotheses generated with and without LLMs; pp. 4 and 13, AI instructions.

confirmed.statement: S3-O1: The four cell means and SDs, all three pairwise p values, and ANOVA F, p and partial eta-squared values match the PDF; the outcome is an individual count of generated hypotheses with AI available.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Experiment 3 results, including the displayed partial eta-squared notation; p. 7, Fig. 2; p. 13, procedure.

confirmed.statement: S3-O2: Accurate hypotheses are counted per participant with AI available; both main-effect p values, the interaction p = .031 and the cross-cell p = .977 match the source.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, last sentence of Experiment 3 results; pp. 5 and 13, scoring and procedure.

confirmed.statement: S3-O3: The objective hit-rate formula and participant unit are supported; the Exp3 LLM point is higher with nearly touching CIs. The form correctly preserves the conflict between the Fig. 4 caption and its plotted total-hypothesis means.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6 and 8; p. 9, Fig. 4(a)-(b) and caption; repeated caption on p. 17.

confirmed.statement: S3-O4: The stated crowd measure is an aggregate count across people, supporting diversity, category_count, set and across_people; the form acknowledges that pooling of incentive cells is unspecified.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Homogeneity of hypotheses generated with and without LLMs; p. 6, factorial design.

confirmed.statement: S4-O1: The scored outcome totals both stages, supporting participant-level fluency with mixed AI availability; it is not a separate unassisted after_ai score. All means, SDs and tests match, and Fig. 3 shows the two single-star comparisons recorded in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Experiment 4 results; p. 8, Fig. 3; p. 13, Experiment 4 procedure.

confirmed.statement: S4-O2: The accurate-hypothesis count compares any-stage LLM use with no use in either stage; all reported means, SDs, t, p and d match the PDF, with a participant unit and mixed availability.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, final Experiment 4 result paragraph; p. 13, stage instructions.

confirmed.statement: S4-O3: Hit rate is computed objectively per participant. The Exp4 points in Fig. 4(a) agree with the printed pooled totals and accurate counts; the form explicitly identifies the extension of that grouping to Fig. 4(b) as an inference.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8; p. 9, Fig. 4(a)-(b); p. 13, cumulative two-stage procedure.

confirmed.statement: S4-O4: The crowd-level distinct-team analysis and no-difference statement are supported; set and diversity distinguish this from individual fluency or flexibility. The source does not specify how its four cells are grouped, as the form notes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Homogeneity of hypotheses generated with and without LLMs; p. 13, four-cell design.

confirmed.statement: S5-O1 is already present in the form. Its occupation-guessing description, fluency name, treatment-higher result and absence of reported numbers match the short source passage; no additional distinct creativity or diversity outcome was identified in the supplied document.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Discussion, ancillary experiment paragraph; full markdown lines 1-240 and PDF pp. 1-17.

confirmed.statement: Confidence is a participants estimate of how many listed teams will qualify; calibration subtracts objective accuracy from that self-report. Their omission from purely output-scored outcomes is supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, confidence question and calculation; p. 8, confidence and calibration definitions; p. 9, Fig. 4(c)-(d).

confirmed.statement: The entire 240-line markdown and all 17 PDF pages were checked; the PDF has no embedded files and no SI Appendix. SI-dependent details remain unverified after direct urllib requests to OSF and SSRN both failed with WinError 10013.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1-17; SI references on pp. 5 and 11-13; retrieval.json c137; read-only source requests during this check.

summary: Criterion 3 holds, and the recorded numerical results match the PDF. Coding is refuted by unsupported accuracy measure labels, an unstated betting-odds decision rule, and unverified scoring and AI timing for the ancillary experiment.
